A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LIDDIA study. All 25 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, support comparison despite substantial reformatting and section relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original molecule-generation experiments on 30 protein targets, baseline comparisons, ablations, toxicity predictions, and molecular case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports detailed EGFR comparisons and token-use/cost estimates.

M1.justification: The REASONER, EXECUTOR, EVALUATOR, and MEMORY architecture remains unchanged, including Pocket2Mol generation, GraphGA optimization, screening, and feedback-based action selection. Wording refinements do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 30 protein targets and disease coverage, including AR/NR3C4 and EGFR. The new discussion of existing benchmarks and EGFR drug resistance does not introduce an evaluated dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: v3 adds Gefitinib as an explicit reference comparator in the EGFR comparison in Figure A1; v2's corresponding performance discussion focuses on Olmutinib and Masoprocol. The benchmark methods, including TargetDiff, DecompDiff, and LIDDIA variants in Table A3, are unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported metrics, thresholds, 10-action limit, Pocket2Mol sampling settings, and deterministic-loop ablation procedure remain unchanged. TargetDiff still uses 29 targets. The expanded EGFR results do not establish revised generation settings or a changed experimental sample.

E4.justification: v3 expands the existing EGFR case study with a 12-molecule comparison across VNA, QED, and SAS in Figure A1. The backend and deterministic-loop ablations, trajectory analysis, failure analysis, toxicity predictions, and AR case study were already present in v2.

E5.justification: Both versions report aggregate results without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. No statistical reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables A2 and A3 retain identical numerical results, including LIDDIA's 73.3% target success rate. v3 adds EGFR comparison outcomes and token/cost estimates. It also changes the prose claim 'NVT and VNA >95%' to 'SAS and VNA >95%', contradicting the retained SAS value of 88.3%.

T1.justification: The novelty, diversity, high-quality-molecule, and target-success definitions in Section 4.1 are mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs that are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the principal performance, autonomous-reasoning, and AR/NR3C4 claims. The conclusion changes its highlighted outcome from one promising AR/NR3C4 molecule to the drug-candidate potential of generated EGFR molecules.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.1 explains dataset curation through existing benchmarks' nonhuman proteins and missing known-drug references. The EGFR discussion adopts a more favorable interpretation of the candidates, while retaining the structural concerns and requirements for expert and experimental validation. The relocated limitations are otherwise unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix C.4 reports approximately 9K input and 5K output tokens per target and an estimated $0.03 cost based on Claude pricing. These resource details were absent from v2. Core implementation settings, prompts, and the code/data access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chen et al. (2024), Huang et al. (2024), Francoeur et al. (2020), and Das et al. (2024) to support backend choice, dataset curation, and EGFR motivation. It removes the Guo et al. DeepSeek-R1 citation. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the narrative: agent analysis precedes ablations, appendix trajectory analysis and the AR case study enter the main results, and limitations move into Section 8. Appendices are reorganized, and the EGFR discussion is expanded and rewritten.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns. An expanded Table 2 replaces the main comparison plots using results already available in v2. Existing figures are split and relocated, appendix case-study figures enter the main text, and a new EGFR comparison grid appears as Figure A1.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves transparency by explaining benchmark selection, documenting resource use, and making the EGFR comparisons more directly assessable. These address limited documentation gaps while preserving the core evidence. The gains are tempered by the new SAS percentage error and more favorable EGFR framing despite retained structural concerns; they do not amount to stronger experimental validation.
